chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrat al-Tamattu', then stood at Arafat and stood at Al-Mash'ar, and threw the Jamarat, and sacrificed, and shaved [his head]. Should he cover his head? He said: No, until he performs Tawaf with the House and with As-Safa and Al-Marwah. It was said to him: If he did [shave before Tawaf], he said: I do not see any blame upon him.

key_terms.الجَمَرَة: Al-Jamarat (the Stoning of the Jamarat pillars)
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.المَشْعَر: Al-Mash'ar (Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the standing place near Muzdalifah)
key_terms.عمرَة التَمَتُّع: Umrat al-Tamattu' (Umrah of Enjoyment, performed separately from Hajj)
key_terms.عَرَفَة: Arafat (the plain where the pilgrim stands during Hajj)
key_terms.يُغَطِّي رَأْسَهُ: Covering the head (a specific penalty/expiation for shaving early in Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before completing the Sa'i during Umrat al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ritual sequence for Umrat al-Tamattu', specifically addressing whether shaving the head before completing the Sa'i incurs a penalty. The Imam confirms that early shaving does not require covering the head (ghut) or expiation, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the order of rituals during the Hajj season. This ruling underscores the practical ease granted to pilgrims, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on removing hardship in acts of worship.
